blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
• Tissue- A Group of similar cells along with intercellular substances, performs a specific function.
  • These tissues are organized in specific proportions and patterns to form an organ like the stomach, lung, heart, and kidney.
  • When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form an organ system, e.g., the digestive system, respiratory system, etc.
  • In a tissue, cells may be dissimilar in structure and function but they are always similar in origin.
  • Tissue Examples -
TYPES OF TISSUES :

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Stating that all epithelial tissues are involved in protection, ignoring their roles in absorption, secretion, and filtration.
    • Believing striated muscles (skeletal muscles) cannot regenerate (they have limited regeneration capacity).
    • Saying cartilage is found "only in joints" (it is also found in structures like the ear, nose, and trachea).

blocks.title: Question. 1
blocks.question:
Which of the following is not a type of animal tissue?
1. Connective
2. Epithelial
3. Meristematic
4. Muscular
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

Explanation:

  • Meristematic tissue is a type of plant tissue, not animal tissue. It is responsible for the growth of plants through cell division at specific regions like the tips of roots and stems.
blocks.prompt:
Which of the following is not a type of animal tissue?
1. Connective
2. Epithelial
3. Meristematic
4. Muscular

blocks.title: Question. 2
blocks.question:
Which of the following is an example of a simple tissue in animals?

1. Blood
2. Cartilage
3. Bone
4. Squamous epithelium
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

Explanation:

  • Squamous epithelium is an example of simple tissue in animals. It consists of a single layer of flat cells and is involved in processes like diffusion and filtration, often found in areas like the lining of blood vessels and the alveoli of the lungs.

blocks.title: Connective Tissue
blocks.text:
• Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed in the body of complex animals.
  • They are named connective tissue because of their special function of linking and supporting other tissues/organs of the body.

blocks.title: The Functions of Connective Tissues are
blocks.text:
The functions of connective tissues are :

1. To connect structures.

2. To form packing around organs.

3. To form a supporting framework.

4. To replace tissues which have been destroyed by injury.

Specialised Connective Tissue :

BLOOD :

• Blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC) and platelets.

• It is the main circulating fluid that helps in the transport of various substances.

blocks.question:
Choose the correctly matched pair :-

(1) Tendon–Specialized connective tissue

(2) Adipose tissue – Dense connective tissue

(3) Areolar tissue – Loose connective tissue

(4) Cartilage–Loose connective tissue
blocks.answer:
Answer- 3

Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue that provides cushioning and support for organs and other tissues.

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
Given below are two statements. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Statement I : Ligaments are dense irregular tissue.

Statement II : Cartilage is dense regular tissue.

(1) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

(2) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

(3) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
blocks.answer:
Answer- 1

Explanation:

  • Statement I: Ligaments are not dense irregular tissue, but dense regular connective tissue, as their collagen fibers are aligned in a parallel arrangement to resist tensile forces in one direction.
  • Statement II: Cartilage is not dense regular tissue, but is a type of supporting connective tissue with a firm, flexible structure that doesn't have the regular arrangement of fibers found in dense regular tissue.
options: (1) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
(2) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
(3) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
(4) Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

blocks.title: Muscle Tissue
blocks.text:
• Each muscle is made of many long, cylindrical fibres arranged in parallel arrays.
  • These fibres are composed of numerous fine fibrils, called myofibrils.
  • Muscle fibres contract (shorten) in response to stimulation, then relax (lengthen) and return to their uncontracted state in a coordinated fashion.
  • Their action moves the body to adjust to the changes in the environment and to maintain the positions of the various parts of the body.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• While ATP is the main energy source, muscles also use creatine phosphate and anaerobic pathways during short bursts of activity.

    • Smooth muscle is non-striated; only skeletal and cardiac muscles are striated.

blocks.question:
Select the incorrectly matched pair from following:

(1) Chondrocytes - Smooth muscle cells

(2) Neurons - Nerve cells

(3) Fibroblast - Areolar tissue

(4) Osteocytes - Bone cells
blocks.answer:
The incorrectly matched pair is:

(1) Chondrocytes - Smooth muscle cells

Explanation:

  • Chondrocytes are the cells found in cartilage, not smooth muscle.
  • Smooth muscle cells are specialized muscle cells responsible for involuntary movements, and they are not the same as chondrocytes.

blocks.question:
Skeletal tissue originated from which embryonic germinal layer :-

(1) Ectoderm

(2) Mesoderm

(3) Endoderm

(4) All the above
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

blocks.title: Nervous Tissue
blocks.text:
• Neural tissue exerts the greatest control over the body’s responsiveness to changing conditions.
  • Neurons, the unit of the neural system, are excitable cells.
  • The neuroglial cells which constitute the rest of the neural system protect and support neurons.
  • Neuroglia make up more than one half the volume of neural tissue in our body.
ORGAN AND ORGAN SYSTEM

Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contributes to the survival of the body as a whole.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text: • Believing axons carry only motor signals and dendrites only carry sensory signals.

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
The cells in the nervous tissue that provide support and protection to neurons are:
(1) Axons
(2) Dendrites
(3) Neuroglial cells
(4) Nissl's bodies
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

Neuroglial cells (or simply glial cells) provide support, protection, and nourishment to neurons. They also play a role in maintaining homeostasis and facilitating signal transmission.
blocks.prompt: The cells in the nervous tissue that provide support and protection to neurons are:

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.question:
Which of the following is a component of nervous tissue?
(1) Osteocyte
(2) Chondrocyte
(3) Neuron
(4) Myocyte
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

Neurons are the functional units of nervous tissue responsible for transmitting electrical signals. The other options—osteocyte, chondrocyte, and myocyte—are components of bone, cartilage, and muscle tissue, respectively.

blocks.title: General Characteristics
blocks.text:
• Brown or black bodied animals.
  • Size ranges from ¼ inches to 3 inches (0.6-7.6 cm)
  • Nocturnal,omnivores,cursorial insects.
  • Adult Periplaneta americana: about 34-53 mm long with wings.
  • Body is divided into head,thorax and abdomen.

blocks.text:
Body = Head + Thorax + Abdomen

6+ 3+ 11= 20 segments in embryo

1+ 3+ 10 = 14 segments in adults

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
Q.1 The terga, sterna and pleura of cockroach body are joined by :-

(1) Muscular tissue

(2) Arthrodial membrane

(3) Cartilage

(4) Cementing glue
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

In a cockroach, the terga (dorsal plates), sterna (ventral plates), and pleura (lateral plates) are joined by a flexible and elastic arthrodial membrane, which allows movement between these rigid structures. This flexibility is essential for the cockroach's mobility and adaptability.

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
Characteristic of group insecta is :

(1) Joined appendages

(2) 3 pair of jointed legs

(3) Chitinous exoskeleton

(4) Compound eyes
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

The defining characteristic of the class Insecta is the presence of three pairs of jointed legs (a total of six legs). This is a key feature that distinguishes insects from other arthropods.

blocks.title: Question-3
blocks.question:
Cockroaches are brown or black bodied animals that are included in class _______ of phylum _______.

(1) reptilia; annelida

(2) insecta; arthropoda

(3) insecta; annelida

(4) reptilia; arthropoda
blocks.answer:
Ans-2

  • Cockroaches belong to the class Insecta, which is characterized by having three pairs of jointed legs, a body divided into three regions (head, thorax, abdomen), compound eyes, and one pair of antennae.
  • They are part of the phylum Arthropoda, which includes animals with a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages, and a segmented body.

blocks.title: General Points
blocks.text:
• Triangular head at 90° to longitudinal axis of body(Hypognathus condition)
  • Movable in all directions.
  • Formed by fusion of six segments to form Head Capsule. The head capsule bears a pair of compound eyes.
  • Each compound eye made up of 2000 units called "ommatidia"
  • Antennae have sensory receptors that help in monitoring the environment. These are the main receptor of touch, temperature,vibration in cockroach.
  • Anterior end of the head bears appendages forming biting and chewing type of mouth parts.
  • The mouthparts consisting of a labrum (upper lip), a pair of mandibles, a pair of maxillae and a labium (lower lip).

blocks.question:

(1) Labrum

(2) Clypeus

(3) Labium

(4) Forehead or frons
blocks.answer:
1

The labrum is a movable chitinous plate that is attached to the dorsal part of the head in cockroaches and other insects. It acts like an upper lip, covering the mouthparts and helping in manipulating food during feeding.

blocks.title: Thorax
blocks.text:
• Thorax consists of three parts – prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax.
  • The head is connected with thorax by a short extension of the prothorax known as the neck.
  • The thorax bears three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings.

blocks.title: Legs
blocks.text:
• 3-pairs of legs (6 legs)
    • Eeach leg is formed of five main segments
(a) segment - "Coxa" :- broadest segment

(b) segment - trochanter :- small segment

(c) long segment - femur

(d) tibia - longest segment

(e) tarsus

    • Tactile setae present on each segment of legs.
    • In Blatta - arolium is absent.
    • Arolium or Pulvilus :- These are adhesive pads
    • Small pads present in between of tarsus segment called "Plantuli"

rows: Covers the hind wings at rest

blocks.title: Points To Remember
blocks.text:
• Locomotion on rough surface: with the help of claws
  • Locomotion on smooth surface : with the help of arolium
  • Climb on the wall : with the help of arolium and plantuli

blocks.question:
Q.1  Tegmina in cockroach, arises from:

(1) Mesothorax

(2) Metathorax

(3) Prothorax and Mesothorax

(4) Prothorax
blocks.answer:
1

The tegmina in cockroaches are the tough, leathery forewings that serve as protective covers for the delicate hindwings. These forewings arise from the mesothorax, the middle segment of the thorax.

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
Q.Select the incorrect statements about the hind wings of cockroach :-

I. These are broad.

II. They are not used in flying

III. They are also known as mesothoracic wings

IV.They are transparent and membranous

(1) Only I

(2) II and III

(3) I and IV

(4) I, II, III and IV
blocks.answer:
Ans- 2

True: Hind wings of cockroaches are broad to assist in flight.

False: Hind wings are used in flying; they are functional wings in cockroaches.

False: Hind wings are not called mesothoracic wings. The mesothoracic wings are the forewings (tegmina), not the hind wings.

True: Hind wings are transparent and membranous to facilitate flight.

blocks.title: Question-3
blocks.question:
Number of segments in cockroach leg :

(1) 3

(2) 5

(3) 6

(4) 9
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

The leg of a cockroach is divided into six segments, which are:

  • Coxa: The basal segment that connects the leg to the thorax.
  • Trochanter: The small segment that acts as a joint between the coxa and femur.
  • Femur: The largest segment, responsible for strength and movement.
  • Tibia: The long, slender segment that supports walking and running.
  • Tarsus: A segmented structure made up of five tarsomeres, aiding in grip and movement.
  • Pretarsus: The terminal segment, which includes claws and a pad-like structure called the arolium for attachment to surfaces.

blocks.text:
• Secretion of peritrophic membrane- by the wall of midgut.

  • Maximum digestion occurs in Crop region
  • Maximum water absorption done in rectum by rectal papilla.

blocks.title: Common Confusions
blocks.text:
• Cockroaches are omnivorous but may occasionally consume plant material. Their diet typically consists of insects, worms, and small invertebrates.
    • Identification of food with the help of an Antenna.
    • The wall of the mesenteron secretes a membrane around food called the peritrophic membrane. It serves to protect the wall of the midgut from friction with hard food particles (permeable to digestive enzymes and food).
    • Mistaking the small intestine for the large intestine in terms of nutrient absorption.
    • Digestion completes in anterior part of midgut.
    • Absorption mainly occurs in posterior part of midgut.

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
In cockroach, identify the parts of the foregut in correct sequence: -

(1) Mouth → Oesophagus → Pharynx →Crop → Gizzard

(2) Mouth → Crop → Pharynx →Oesophagus → Gizzard

(3) Mouth → Gizzard → Crop → Pharynx→ Oesophagus

(4) Mouth → Pharynx → Oesophagus →Crop → Gizzard
blocks.answer:
Answer:4

The foregut of a cockroach consists of the following parts in this order:

  • Mouth: The entry point for food.
  • Pharynx: A muscular portion that helps in the passage of food.
  • Oesophagus: The tube that connects the pharynx to the crop.
  • Crop: A storage area where food is temporarily stored before further digestion.
  • Gizzard: A muscular part that grinds and crushes the food.
Thus, the correct sequence of the foregut in a cockroach is Mouth → Pharynx → Oesophagus → Crop → Gizzard.

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
What is the primary role of the gizzard in the cockroach?
1) Digestion of proteins
2) Grinding food
3) Absorption of nutrients
4) Secretion of digestive enzymes
blocks.answer:
Answer: 2) Grinding food

The primary role of the gizzard in the cockroach is to grind the food into finer particles using its thick muscular walls and chitinous teeth or plates. This aids in mechanical digestion before the food moves further into the digestive tract.

blocks.title: Circulatory System
blocks.text:
• Open type
  • Haemocoel cavity present
  • Haemolymph consists of colorless plasma and haematocytes.
  • Dorsal, tubular and 13 chambered heart.
  • Alary muscles:fused with heart wall and helps in maintaining blood circulation

blocks.title: Excretory System
blocks.text:
• Cockroach is Uricotelic.
  • Excretion is done by Malpighian tubules(main excretory structure).
  • Other structure involved in excretion:Fat body, nephrocytes and uricose glands and the body wall.
  • Malpighian tubules are100-150 in number,found at the junction of midgut and hindgut. They are lined by glandular and ciliated epithelium.
  • Uricose gland helps in excretion in the male cockroach only.

blocks.title: Nervous System
blocks.text:
• Consists of a series of fused, segmentally arranged ganglia.
  • The sense organs are antennae, eyes, maxillary palps, labial palps, anal cerci, etc.
  • Each compound eye consists of about 2000 hexagonal units called ommatidia.
  • Mosaic vision (more sensitivity but less resolution),nocturnal vision

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.text:
• Overlooking that the rectum helps conserve water.
    • Cockroaches are uricotelic, meaning they excrete nitrogenous waste primarily as 'potassium urate', which conserves water.
    • Malpighian tubules filter hemolymph. They remove nitrogenous waste (mainly uric acid) and help in osmoregulation by excreting waste into the hindgut.
    • Antennae are sensitive to touch and smell, while compound eyes detect motion and light.

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
Q.1 Give the name of blood vessel, which arises from first chamber of heart in cockroach :

(1) Nephrocyte

(2) Fenestrae

(3) Ostia

(4) Anterior aorta
blocks.answer:
Answer:4

In a cockroach, the anterior aorta is the blood vessel that arises from the first chamber of the heart (the dorsal vessel). It is responsible for carrying haemolymph (the blood-like fluid) to the head and other anterior parts of the body.
blocks.prompt: Q.1 Give the name of blood vessel, which arises from first chamber of heart in cockroach :

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
Q.2 Main excretory product of cockroach is :

(1) Urea       (2) Ammonia

(3) Uric acid    (4) Amino acid
blocks.answer:
Answer: 3

Explanation:

  • Cockroaches are uricotelic, meaning their main excretory product is uric acid.
  • Uric acid is insoluble in water and is excreted as a paste or solid, which helps conserve water, an important adaptation for terrestrial life.
blocks.prompt: Q.2 Main excretory product of cockroach is :

blocks.title: Question- 3
blocks.question:
Q.3 The nerve cord of cockroach is :

(1) Double, ventral and solid

(2) Double dorsal and hollow

(3) Single, dorsal and solid

(4) Single, ventral and hollow
blocks.answer:
Answer:1

Explanation:

  • In cockroaches, the nerve cord is double, meaning it consists of two longitudinal nerve cords.
  • It is located ventrally (on the underside of the body).
  • Unlike the nerve cord in vertebrates (which is hollow), the cockroach nerve cord is solid.

    • Cockroaches are uricotelic, meaning they excrete nitrogenous waste primarily as 'potassium urate', which conserves water.
    • Malpighian tubules filter hemolymph. They remove nitrogenous waste (mainly uric acid) and help in osmoregulation by excreting waste into the hindgut.
    • Antennae are sensitive to touch and smell, while compound eyes detect motion and light.

blocks.title: Legs
blocks.text:
• 3-pairs of legs (6 legs)
    • Eeach leg is formed of five main segments
(a) segment - "Coxa" :- broadest segment

(b) segment - trochanter :- small segment

(c) long segment - femur

(d) tibia - longest segment

(e) tarsus

    • Tactile setae present on each segment of legs.
    • In Blatta - arolium is absent.
    • Arolium or Pulvilus :- These are adhesive pads
    • Small pads present in between of tarsus segment called "Plantuli"

rows: Covers the hind wings at rest

blocks.title: Excretory System
blocks.text:
• Cockroach is Uricotelic.
  • Excretion is done by Malpighian tubules(main excretory structure).
  • Other structure involved in excretion:Fat body, nephrocytes and uricose glands and the body wall.
  • Malpighian tubules are100-150 in number,found at the junction of midgut and hindgut. They are lined by glandular and ciliated epithelium.
  • Uricose gland helps in excretion in the male cockroach only.
